featured_techniques.technique: Closing with peace of mind / reassurance

sections.description: Introduces the bookends concept and contrasts greeting approaches: transactional vs relational. Emphasizes asking about what the client aims to accomplish in their business rather than defaulting to tax-year or other administrative questions.
sections.title: Deliberate Hello in CX

sections.description: Discusses avoiding purely transactional questions and ending interactions with actions that provide the client peace of mind.
sections.title: Relational Conversation and Peaceful Goodbye

summary: The video frames customer experience around two pivotal moments—the hello and the goodbye. Jeanne Bliss argues that onboarding should start with a deliberate, relationship-focused welcome that asks about what a client wants to accomplish in their business, rather than defaulting to transactional checks such as tax-year questions. She contrasts this with a personal anecdote about an accountant whose interactions felt overly transactional. The outro matters too: a thoughtful goodbye should leave the client with peace of mind and a sense of closure. Taken together, the video promotes a relational, goal-oriented approach to client conversations at both the start and end of interactions, rather than purely transactional exchanges.
title: Customer Experience Bookends: Hello and Goodbye as Deliberate Interactions
